rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people with greater talents and resources by whether they become arrogant, selfish and disobedient or grateful, obedient and sympathetic.
rows.anchor: After benefiting from them, have they been inflicted with arrogance, selfishness, forcibly imposing themselves on others and disobeying the Creator of the worlds or show gratefulness, obedience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people with fewer worldly means by whether they meet their responsibilities, fear their Creator and preserve their self-respect, or neglect their duties and resent their superiors.
rows.anchor: whether they recognize their responsibilities in their spheres of life, fear their Creator and protect their self-esteem and honour

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cooperation between the high and low creates a noble society in which all receive respect and are rewarded in the Hereafter according to service and intention.
rows.anchor: because of the noble co-operation of the high and the low, a noble society comes into being, and all its components without any distinction receive respect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglect and rebellion against social responsibilities gradually disorder and destroy society, and its elements incur divine wrath in proportion to their misconduct.
rows.anchor: the system of the society gradually gives way to disorder and then finally annihilates

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abolishing class differences cannot succeed without equalizing people's mental, natural and practical abilities, which is impossible.
rows.anchor: they are able to make people equal in their mental, temperamental, natural and practical abilities, and this is impossible

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if society's abilities and resources were equalized, mutual cooperation would end and anarchy would spread.
rows.anchor: the basis of mutual cooperation will finish and anarchy will spread in the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase meaning from silver is elided after the stairways, doors and couches because eloquent Arabic permits omission when context strongly indicates it.
rows.anchor: as per linguistic principles of eloquent Arabic they are suppressed because there is a strong indication of its presence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' worldly wealth has no standing before God; their worldly status made them presume revelation should come to someone like themselves.
rows.anchor: how is it possible that God reveal a Book and reveal it to someone other than themselves

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives worldly riches to believers and disbelievers to shield the masses from the severe trial of seeing only disbelievers prosper; the disbelievers gain no share in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has blessed the believers and the disbelievers with worldly riches; however, the disbelievers will have no share in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prediction that people would follow disbelief if only disbelievers were rich is a statement about the generality and the majority, not a universal principle.
rows.anchor: it is given with regard to generality and the majority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even in such a severe trial, some noble souls would preserve their faith and succeed.
rows.anchor: some noble souls who would succeed in the severest of trials

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can mean embellishment and gold, since gold is a means of embellishment.
rows.anchor: The word ز also connotes “embellishment” and also “gold” which is a means of embellishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical reading coordinates the gold phrase with the earlier phrase meaning of silver.
rows.anchor: Grammatically, it can be regarded to be coordinated to the syntactical status of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the gold phrase may be the object of an elided verb, meaning God could make the things gold or gather heaps of gold.
rows.anchor: can also be regarded to be the object of a suppressed verb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two grammatical readings make little difference in meaning.
rows.anchor: There would not be much difference in either of these

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says lammā distinguishes shortened an from negative an, with lām expanded to lammā to maintain rhythm; he cites 86:4.
rows.anchor: which comes to distinguish the shortened ( mukhaffafah) أنْfrom the negative ( nāfiyah) أنْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly adornments are transient; lasting favors belong to the Hereafter, which belongs solely to those who fear God.
rows.anchor: The real everlasting favours will be granted in the Hereafter, and before the Prophet’s Lord, the Hereafter solely belongs to those who fear God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's established practice, a devil becomes the abiding companion of whoever turns away from God's remembrance and leads that person to Hell.
rows.anchor: as per the established practice of God a devil is deputed by God on people who turn away from His remembrance who becomes their abiding companion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ʿashā ʿan al-shayʾ means to show indifference toward something.
rows.anchor: means “to show indifference to something”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God's remembrance inhabits a person's heart, Satan cannot enter; indifference to God lets Satan gradually overcome it.
rows.anchor: as long as the remembrance of God inhabits it, Satan cannot find any way into it; but when a person becomes indifferent to God, Satan slowly vanquishes it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan raises objections to good advice to disillusion people, but cannot remain in hearts saturated with God's remembrance and flees once recognized.
rows.anchor: Satan is able to raise doubts and objections against the best of advice and reminders that come before a person thereby disillusioning him from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is used generically for human and jinn satans, so plural pronouns describe the group caught in their grasp.
rows.anchor: is also used in the general sense. It can refer to both the satans among men and among the jinn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The antecedent of innahum is the satans.
rows.anchor: is the satans and the subject of the verb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of yahsabūn is the people caught in Satan's trap.
rows.anchor: is the people who are caught in the trap of stans

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in pronouns is not a defect when the discourse makes the referents clear; Islahi cites 12:110 as an example.
rows.anchor: In a discourse, whose meaning is evident, such dispersion in pronouns is not a defect

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though such companions seem close in worldly life, the deceived person will curse his companion in the Hereafter and wish they had been separated as far as the two Easts.
rows.anchor: he will curse his companion and would express the wish that he had been as far apart from him as the two Easts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase fabiʾsa al-qarīn expresses God's curse and hatred for the evil companion who pushed his friend into ruin.
rows.anchor: are an expression of curse and hate from the Almighty for the evil companion

rows.speaker: Our exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes generally interpret al-mashriqayn as the East and the West.
rows.anchor: Our exegetes have generally interpreted the word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the East-and-West interpretation; he says the Arabic dual can express the vastness of both sides of a thing.
rows.anchor: in my opinion, this is not correct. At times, in Arabic the dual connotes the vastness of both sides of a thing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment, leaders and followers cannot escape blame by cursing each other: they wronged themselves together, and both must bear torment; the past cannot be recovered.
rows.anchor: This will not absolve either of them from blame; both will have to bear torment now

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's reminders can benefit only those with living faculties of thought and understanding; the deaf and self-blinded cannot be advised this way.
rows.anchor: his advice and reminders can only be effective on those whose faculties of thinking and comprehension are alive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lack of knowledge can be remedied, but guiding someone who openly errs while knowing it is impossible.
rows.anchor: to guide a person who is in open error and is also aware that he is inflicted with this error

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is reassured to leave the wrongdoers: God may take him first and then punish them, or let him witness the promised punishment, for God has full power over them.
rows.anchor: either the Almighty will give death to him and then take revenge from them or the punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite frivolous opposition, the Prophet must adhere firmly to the call to monotheism and the revealed Book; he is rightly guided, while his opponents have no argument and will soon be defeated.
rows.anchor: should strongly adhere to his call to monotheism and this Book which is revealed to him. He only is on the right path

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder for the Prophet and his nation, and every person will be questioned about it.
rows.anchor: is a reminder for him as well as for his nation, and one day each person
